title: Park, Gym, Lights
bigQuestion: Who built the parks, gyms and lighted fields that a whole town shares?

story.title: Lights Before the Game
story.kicker: Tall lights click on over an empty field before anyone arrives.
paragraphs: It is Friday in a small Illinois town. The sun is going down. The football field is empty. The grass looks gray in the dusk.
Click. The tall poles light up, one after another. The grass turns bright green. A worker from the school district walks the track and checks each lamp.
A girl named Rosa waits by the gate with her grandpa. "Who paid for those lights?" she asks. "We all did," he says. "The town voted to build them."
Soon cars fill the lot. The band marches in. Rosa looks at the bleachers, the white lines and the bright poles. Many families shared the cost of this one place.
story.think: Who do you think paid for the gym or field nearest your school?

lessons.title: Boston Common, 1634
lessons.mainIdea: Boston Common, set aside in 1634, is the oldest public park in the United States.
reading: A *public park* is land that belongs to everyone in a town. The oldest one in the United States is Boston Common. Boston set it aside in 1634.
At first, families let their cows eat grass there. Cows grazed on the Common until 1830. Later, children played ball games on the open grass.

words.d: land that belongs to everyone in a town
an open field shared by a whole town

look.title: A Shared Field

check.q: What is a public park?
choices: a club only members may use

check.why: A public park belongs to everyone in the town.

lessons.title: How Lincoln Park Got Its Name
lessons.mainIdea: Chicago named Lincoln Park in 1865 to honor President Abraham Lincoln.
reading: Lincoln Park sits along Lake Michigan in Chicago. Part of the land was once a city cemetery. In 1860, Chicago began turning it into a park.
President Abraham Lincoln was killed in April 1865. That same year, Chicago named the park to *honor* him. People still walk its paths today.
In 1868, a zoo opened in the park. New York's Central Park sent two swans as a gift. Lincoln Park Zoo is still free to visit.

words.d: to show respect for a person, such as by naming a place for them

look.title: Two Names, One Place
look.text: Before 1865, some people called this land Lake Park. Then President Lincoln died. The city gave the park his name. The grass and trees stayed the same. Only the name changed.

check.why: To honor someone is to show respect, such as by naming a place for them.

lessons.title: One Park District for Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1934, 22 small park districts joined to make the Chicago Park District.
reading: A *park district* is a local government that runs parks. Long ago, Chicago had many small park districts. In 1934, 22 of them joined into one.
The new group was the Chicago Park District. Today it runs more than 600 parks. It also runs beaches, pools and Soldier Field.
Park districts get money from local *taxes*. Taxes are money people pay to share costs. Many Illinois towns have their own park district.

words.d: a local government that runs parks, pools and playing fields
money people pay to a government to share the cost of things everyone uses

lessons.title: A Greek Word
lessons.mainIdea: Gym is short for gymnasium, a place for exercise in ancient Greece.
reading: The word *gym* is short for gymnasium. The word comes from ancient Greece. More than 2,000 years ago, Greek cities built gymnasiums.
A Greek gymnasium had open yards and covered walkways. Young men ran and trained there. Teachers taught there too. Plato taught at one near Athens.
Most Greek gymnasiums were only for boys and men. Girls and women were kept out. Today, a public school gym is for every student.

words.d: a room or building for exercise and games; short for gymnasium

look.text: At Olympia in Greece, you can still see what is left of an old gymnasium. Rows of stone columns stand in the grass. Athletes trained here long ago, before the games.

check.why: Gym is short for gymnasium, a Greek word.

check.q: Which teacher taught at a gymnasium near Athens?

lessons.title: A Winter Gym in Springfield
lessons.mainIdea: James Naismith made up basketball in a Springfield gym in December 1891.
reading: James Naismith was a teacher from Canada. In 1891, he taught at a *YMCA* school in Springfield, Massachusetts. Winter kept his class inside.
Naismith needed a game for that indoor room. In December 1891, two peach baskets were nailed to a balcony. They hung 10 feet high.
That was the start of basketball. The gym shaped the new game. The hoop is still 10 feet high today.

words.d: the Young Men's Christian Association, a group that built gyms in many cities

look.title: Boxes or Baskets
look.text: Naismith later wrote that his class needed a game they could play indoors in winter. He asked a worker for two boxes. The worker brought two old peach baskets instead.
look.cite: James Naismith, Basketball: Its Origin and Development (1941)
look.prompt: What did Naismith ask for, and what did he get?

check.q: Why was Naismith's class inside?
check.why: Winter kept the class in the gym.

check.q: How high did the first baskets hang?
check.why: The peach baskets hung 10 feet high, like hoops today.

check.q: In what year did basketball begin?
check.why: Naismith started the game in December 1891.

lessons.title: Fieldhouses in the Parks
lessons.mainIdea: In 1905, new Chicago parks opened with fieldhouses that held a gym for the neighborhood.
reading: A *fieldhouse* is a building in a park. It can hold a gym, showers and meeting rooms. Some Chicago fieldhouses held small libraries too.
In 1905, new parks opened on Chicago's South Side. They were among the first parks in the country with fieldhouses. Families could use them for free.
Jane Addams also worked for places to play. In the 1890s, her Hull-House opened a playground on Chicago's Near West Side.

words.d: a building in a park with a gym and other rooms for the neighborhood

look.title: Three Doors
look.text: Picture a brick building in a Chicago park in 1905. One door leads to a gym. One leads to warm showers. One leads to a room full of books. Many homes nearby have no bathtub.
look.prompt: Why might a crowded neighborhood want all these rooms in one building?

check.q: What is a fieldhouse?
choices: a building in a park with a gym

check.q: When did the new South Side parks open?
check.why: They opened in 1905 with fieldhouses.

check.q: Who ran Hull-House?
check.why: Jane Addams ran Hull-House, which opened a playground in the 1890s.

lessons.title: The First Big-League Night Game
lessons.mainIdea: The first major league baseball game under lights was played in Cincinnati in 1935.
reading: In 1879, Thomas Edison made a light bulb that lasted many hours. Still, most big games stayed in daylight for years. When the sun set, play stopped.
On May 24, 1935, the Cincinnati Reds played at night. It was the first *major league* game under lights. President Franklin Roosevelt turned them on. He pressed a button in Washington.
Night games let working people come after their jobs. Over the next years, more ballparks put up lights.

words.d: the top level of paid baseball in the United States and Canada

check.q: Where was the first major league night game?
check.why: The Cincinnati Reds played the first major league night game in 1935.

check.q: Who turned on the lights from Washington?
check.why: President Roosevelt pressed a button in Washington.

check.q: Why did night games help working people?
choices: they could come after their jobs
check.why: Night games started after most work days ended.

lessons.title: Wrigley Field Turns On Lights
lessons.mainIdea: Wrigley Field in Chicago added lights in 1988, the last major league park to do so.
reading: Wrigley Field opened on Chicago's North Side in 1914. The Cubs have played there since 1916. For many years, every home game was in the daytime.
Some neighbors did not want night games. They worried about noise and crowds. The Cubs were the last major league team to add lights at their *ballpark*.
The lights went on in August 1988. The first full night game was on August 9, 1988. The Cubs beat the New York Mets.

words.d: a park built for baseball games, with a field and seats
